plan: Trim SPY to 20% to meet the concentration mandate and reduce broad index exposure.
Sell all SOXL and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETF risk, aligning with capital preservation.
Trim QQQI and QQQ to reduce overall market exposure and free up capital.
Sell SMH due to its downtrend and negative P&L, removing a weaker holding.
Buy XLV at 5% to diversify into a top-quality, non-tech sector setup.
Maintain a significant cash buffer by reducing overall portfolio size.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for capital preservation, targeting around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and potential drawdown by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to align with the concentration mandate and reduce overall risk.
Sell SOXL and SPAL to remove high-risk leveraged ETFs from the portfolio.
Sell QQQI and SMH due to their downtrends and scanner flags, improving portfolio quality.
Trim QQQ to reduce broad index exposure and free up capital for new opportunities.
Add to CRWD, an uptrending AI/Software holding, to press a working position.
Buy AAPL at 10% as a top-quality tech setup from the scanner list, diversifying tech exposure.
balanced.read: This balanced approach prioritizes risk-first growth, aiming for approximately 2.5% per month. It reduces high-risk leverage and concentration while adding to quality tech, aiming for moderate growth with managed drawdown.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate while maintaining significant broad exposure.
Sell SOXL, SPAL, QQQI, and SMH to remove all flagged and downtrending positions, freeing capital.
Trim QQQ to reduce broad index exposure, reallocating to higher conviction setups.
Add significantly to CRWD, an uptrending AI/Software name, to press a working position.
Buy AAPL at 15% and AAPU at 10% as high-scoring, top-quality long setups from the scanner.
This strategy uses available leverage for growth in strong setups, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth approach targets around 4% per month, leaning into leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups. It carries a significantly higher risk of drawdown, amplified by leverage and potential decay in any future leveraged ETF additions. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

moves.note: Exit broad index for income focus

plan: Trim SPY to 15% to reduce broad market exposure and maintain some diversification.
Sell all SOXL, SPAL, QQQ, SMH, and CRWD to eliminate leveraged, high-beta, and non-income assets.
Significantly add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 40% for enhanced monthly distributions.
This rotation prioritizes income and low drawdown by focusing on income-generating ETFs.
Maintain a cash buffer by reducing overall portfolio size and high-risk holdings.
income.read: This income-focused approach targets approximately 1% per month from distributions, prioritizing yield and low drawdown. While aiming for steady income, distributions are variable and the NAV can still decline in market selloffs. This is not a savings account and some market risk remains.
